question: For the matrix $$A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{bmatrix},$$ evaluate the matrix expression $A^2-4A+3I$, where $I$ is the identity matrix of order $2$, and establish that the resulting matrix is the zero matrix.
explanation:
Evaluation of the Matrix Power

We first calculate $A^2=A\cdot A$. Thus, $$A^2=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\cdot2+1\cdot1&2\cdot1+1\cdot2\\1\cdot2+2\cdot1&1\cdot1+2\cdot2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}5&4\\4&5\end{bmatrix}$$ Also, $$4A=\begin{bmatrix}8&4\\4&8\end{bmatrix}$$ and, since $I=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$, $$3I=\begin{bmatrix}3&0\\0&3\end{bmatrix}$$

Simplification

Therefore, $$A^2-4A+3I=\begin{bmatrix}5&4\\4&5\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}8&4\\4&8\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}3&0\\0&3\end{bmatrix}$$ $$=\begin{bmatrix}5-8+3&4-4+0\\4-4+0&5-8+3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}$$ The matrix obtained has every element equal to zero and is therefore the zero matrix. Hence, $$A^2-4A+3I=O$$ as required.
